use: Mostly in complaints: 'matomo na shigoto' (a proper job), 'matomo ja nai' (not normal).

example.romaji: Kinou kara matomo na mono tabete nai.
example.ja: 昨日からまともなもの食べてない。
example.english: I haven't had a proper meal since yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou kara matomo na mono o tabete imasen.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日からまともなものを食べていません。
examplePolite.english: I haven't eaten a proper meal since yesterday.

notes: 'Matomo ni' means properly: 'matomo ni hanasenai' (can't even talk properly).

use: Usually 'seishiki ni' (officially) or 'seishiki na' before a noun.

example.romaji: Mada seishiki ni kimatta wake ja nai yo.
example.ja: まだ正式に決まったわけじゃないよ。
example.english: It's not officially decided yet.

examplePolite.romaji: Mada seishiki ni wa kimatte imasen.
examplePolite.ja: まだ正式には決まっていません。
examplePolite.english: It hasn't been officially decided yet.

use: Mostly 'akiraka ni' (clearly, obviously).

example.romaji: Sore, akiraka ni uso da yo.
example.ja: それ、明らかに嘘だよ。
example.english: That's obviously a lie.

examplePolite.romaji: Sore wa akiraka ni uso desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それは明らかに嘘ですよ。
examplePolite.english: That's clearly a lie.

notes: 'Atarimae' is 'of course, naturally'; 'akiraka' is 'plain to see'.

use: Sounds formal; everyday talk uses 'dekiru' instead.

example.romaji: Sore tte, honto ni kanou na no?
example.ja: それって、ほんとに可能なの？
example.english: Is that even possible?

examplePolite.romaji: Kyoujuu ni kanou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今日中に可能ですか。
examplePolite.english: Is it possible by the end of today?

use: For jokes, shows or arguments not worth your time.

example.romaji: Sonna kudaranai koto de kenka shinaide.
example.ja: そんなくだらないことでけんかしないで。
example.english: Don't fight over something so stupid.

examplePolite.romaji: Sonna kudaranai koto de kenka shinaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: そんなくだらないことでけんかしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't argue over something so trivial.

notes: Often said 'kudannai'. About a silly joke it can be affectionate: 'Kudaranai!' (So dumb!).

use: For size, temperature, amount or timing.

example.romaji: Kono saizu, choudo ii.
example.ja: このサイズ、ちょうどいい。
example.english: This size is just right.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono saizu ga choudo ii desu.
examplePolite.ja: このサイズがちょうどいいです。
examplePolite.english: This size is just right.

notes: Changes like 'ii': 'choudo yokatta' (that worked out perfectly).

politeJa: どうしようもありません
english: hopeless, nothing can be done; useless (person)
use: About a situation: nothing can be done; about a person: hopeless.

example.romaji: Ame da kara, dou shiyou mo nai ne.
example.ja: 雨だから、どうしようもないね。
example.english: It's raining, nothing we can do.

examplePolite.romaji: Ame na node, dou shiyou mo arimasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 雨なので、どうしようもありませんね。
examplePolite.english: It's raining, so there's nothing we can do.

notes: 'Shou ga nai' is the everyday 'oh well'; 'dou shiyou mo nai' is stronger: truly hopeless.

use: For colours and clothes, and for people or lifestyles that stand out.

example.romaji: Sono shatsu, chotto hade ja nai?
example.ja: そのシャツ、ちょっと派手じゃない？
example.english: Isn't that shirt a bit loud?

examplePolite.romaji: Sono shatsu, chotto hade ja nai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: そのシャツ、ちょっと派手じゃないですか。
examplePolite.english: Isn't that shirt a little flashy?

use: About a person it means easily led or naive, often teasing.

example.romaji: Kare, tanjun da kara sugu shinjiru yo.
example.ja: 彼、単純だからすぐ信じるよ。
example.english: He's gullible, he'll believe it right away.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa tanjun na node, sugu shinjimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は単純なので、すぐ信じますよ。
examplePolite.english: He's quite naive, so he'll believe it right away.

notes: For a simple design or plan, 'shinpuru' is the positive word.

use: Often after a te-form: 'itte mo imi nai' (no point saying it).

example.romaji: Imasara isoide mo imi nai yo.
example.ja: 今さら急いでも意味ないよ。
example.english: No point hurrying now.

examplePolite.romaji: Imasara isoide mo imi ga arimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: 今さら急いでも意味がありませんよ。
examplePolite.english: There's no point hurrying now.

use: Mostly 'gutaiteki ni' (specifically); 'Gutaiteki ni wa?' asks 'Like what, exactly?'

example.romaji: Gutaiteki ni nani ga dame na no?
example.ja: 具体的に何がだめなの？
example.english: What exactly is wrong with it?

examplePolite.romaji: Gutaiteki ni nani ga dame na n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 具体的に何がだめなんですか。
examplePolite.english: What specifically is the problem?

use: 'Fukuzatsu na kimochi' means mixed feelings.

example.romaji: Kono setsumei, fukuzatsu de wakannai yo.
example.ja: この説明、複雑でわかんないよ。
example.english: This explanation is too complicated, I don't get it.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono setsumei wa fukuzatsu de wakarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この説明は複雑でわかりません。
examplePolite.english: This explanation is too complicated to follow.

use: 'Kojinteki ni wa' (personally, for me) softens an opinion.

example.romaji: Kojinteki ni wa, kotchi no hou ga suki.
example.ja: 個人的には、こっちの方が好き。
example.english: Personally, I like this one better.

examplePolite.romaji: Kojinteki ni wa, kochira no hou ga suki desu.
examplePolite.ja: 個人的には、こちらの方が好きです。
examplePolite.english: Personally, I prefer this one.

use: For drinks and food it means bland or watered down.

example.romaji: Kono koohii, chotto usui ne.
example.ja: このコーヒー、ちょっと薄いね。
example.english: This coffee's a bit weak.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono koohii, chotto usui desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: このコーヒー、ちょっと薄いですね。
examplePolite.english: This coffee is a little weak.

notes: Opposite for taste and colour: 'koi'; for thickness: 'atsui'.

use: Mostly 'something's off': 'nanka okashii' means something's wrong.

example.romaji: Kono kikai, nanka okashii yo.
example.ja: この機械、なんかおかしいよ。
example.english: Something's wrong with this machine.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono kikai, nanika okashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: この機械、何かおかしいです。
examplePolite.english: Something seems wrong with this machine.

notes: Before a noun you also hear 'okashina': 'okashina hanashi' (a strange story). 'Okashi' is sweets.

use: For scarce things: time, chances, experiences, belongings.

example.romaji: Sore, kichou na keiken da ne.
example.ja: それ、貴重な経験だね。
example.english: That's a valuable experience.

examplePolite.romaji: Kichou na keiken deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 貴重な経験でした。
examplePolite.english: It was a valuable experience.

use: Before a noun it means 'typical, common': 'yoku aru hanashi'.

example.romaji: Sore, yoku aru machigai da yo.
example.ja: それ、よくある間違いだよ。
example.english: That's a common mistake.

examplePolite.romaji: Sore wa yoku aru machigai desu.
examplePolite.ja: それはよくある間違いです。
examplePolite.english: That's a common mistake.

use: 'X kusai' means smells of X: 'tabako kusai'.

example.romaji: Nanka kono heya, kusakunai?
example.ja: なんかこの部屋、臭くない？
example.english: Doesn't this room smell?

examplePolite.romaji: Kono heya, chotto kusai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この部屋、ちょっと臭いですね。
examplePolite.english: This room smells a bit.

notes: As an ending it also means '-ish, seems like': 'mendokusai' (a pain), 'uso kusai' (sounds like a lie).

use: 'X yori mashi' means better than X; never real praise.

example.romaji: Kinou yori wa mashi da yo.
example.ja: 昨日よりはマシだよ。
example.english: It's better than yesterday, at least.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou yori wa mashi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日よりはマシです。
examplePolite.english: It's better than yesterday, at least.

notes: 'Mashi na X' is a decent X: 'Mashi na mise nai?' (Anywhere decent around?).

use: For clothes, colours, people and work that don't stand out.

example.romaji: Kyou no fuku, chotto jimi kana.
example.ja: 今日の服、ちょっと地味かな。
example.english: Is my outfit a bit plain today?

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou no fuku wa chotto jimi deshou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 今日の服はちょっと地味でしょうか。
examplePolite.english: Is today's outfit a little plain?
